value.rationale: The long-time entropy covariance and its d^2 scaling are natural quantitative measures of how a shared restoring protocol couples otherwise independent physical degrees of freedom. The exact coefficient distinguishes synchronous and independent reset clocks despite identical one-coordinate laws. The strict Fano excess and nonzero infinite-d relative-variance limit supply experimentally interpretable thermodynamic reliability criteria and cannot be inferred quantitatively from known stationary-density correlations alone. No broader thermodynamic uncertainty law or actuator-energy equivalence is claimed.
